Below are two *SEARCH/REPLACE* edits—one for your C-like grammar and one for JavaScript—to allow underscore separators in all of the various numeric literals.  Both changes replace the old number-matching regex with a new one that permits digits grouped by “_” (but never at the start or end of a number, or next to the decimal point or exponent).

```javascript
### components/prism-clike.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
\t'function': /\w+(?=\()/,
\t'number': /\b0x[\da-f]+\b|(?:\b\d+\.?\d*|\B\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?/i,
\t'operator': /--?|\+\+?|!=?=?|<=?|>=?|==?=?|&&?|\|\|?|\?|[*/~^%]/,
=======
\t'function': /\w+(?=\()/,
\t'number': /\b0x[\da-f]+(?:_[\da-f]+)*\b|(?:\b\d+(?:_\d+)*\.?\d*(?:_\d+)*|\B\.\d+(?:_\d+)*)(?:e[+-]?\d+(?:_\d+)*)?/i,
\t'operator': /--?|\+\+?|!=?=?|<=?|>=?|==?=?|&&?|\|\|?|\?|[*/~^%]/,
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

```javascript
### components/prism-javascript.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
\t'number': /\b(?:(?:0[xX][\dA-Fa-f]+|0[bB][01]+|0[oO][0-7]+)n?|\d+n|NaN|Infinity)\b|(?:\b\d+\.?\d*|\B\.\d+)(?:[Ee][+-]?\d+)?/,
\t// Allow for all non-ASCII characters (See http://stackoverflow.com/a/2008444)
=======
\t'number': /\b(?:(?:0[xX][\dA-Fa-f]+(?:_[\dA-Fa-f]+)*)|(?:0[bB][01]+(?:_[01]+)*)|(?:0[oO][0-7]+(?:_[0-7]+)*))n?|\d+(?:_\d+)*n|NaN|Infinity\b|(?:\b\d+(?:_\d+)*\.?\d*(?:_\d+)*|\B\.\d+(?:_\d+)*)(?:[Ee][+-]?\d+(?:_\d+)*)?/,
\t// Allow for all non-ASCII characters (See http://stackoverflow.com/a/2008444)
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the new patterns:

- Hex (`0x`), binary (`0b`), octal (`0o`) and decimal BigInt literals now allow groups of digits separated by underscores, e.g.  
  `0xFF_FF`, `0b1010_1010`, `123_456n`.

- Decimal floats allow underscores in both integer and fraction parts, e.g.  
  `1_000.220_720`, and still support optional exponents like `1_000e+3_00`.

With these two replacements, Prism will correctly tokenize and highlight any numeric-separator literals.
